patch_description: Instead of a single central circle with two rings (which wastes corner space), I build a multi-scale explicit skeleton: 4 corner circles, an asymmetric perimeter chain (3 circles on the bottom edge, 2 on the others — breaking symmetry helps edge utilization), and a staggered 5-4-5-4 interior hex lattice. Radii are then computed by a Gauss-Seidel min-relaxation fixed point (r_i = min(border, min_j(d_ij - r_j))), which guarantees a valid packing and naturally produces the size grading the skeleton implies (larger corner/edge circles, smaller interior ones — matching the insight that varied radii beat uniform patterns near square boundaries). Finally, a short deterministic "pressure-release" polish loop nudges centers away from tight contacts (overlaps and wall pressures) with decaying step size, re-relaxing radii each step and keeping the best valid configuration. This combines explicit constructor structure with a lightweight geometric refinement rather than a blind search.
